overview: The Energy and Environment Committee reviewed city environmental updates, tracked progress on the Climate Action Plan, and debated proposed changes to municipal waste collection and pay-as-you-throw policies. The committee approved the previous meeting's minutes and discussed legislative initiatives around rodenticide and plastics reduction.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee unanimously voted to accept the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: City Environmental Updates
items.summary: Staff provided updates on upcoming environmental events, the Electrify Medford program, third-party energy supplier costs, revisions to the municipal aggregation plan, air quality sensors at local schools, EV charger installations, and sustainability targets for the high school building project.

items.title: Climate Action Plan Review
items.summary: The committee walked through the Climate Action Plan tracking matrix, discussing municipal progress on zoning recodification, affordable housing trusts, specialized energy code enforcement, and Building Department staffing capacity.

items.title: Member Updates and State Legislation
items.summary: Members discussed state legislative items under the Mass Ready Act, including proposed bans and restrictions on anticoagulant rodenticides, plastics reduction measures, and dark sky lighting legislation.

items.title: Pay-As-You-Throw and Waste Management Discussion
items.summary: The committee debated a proposal for bi-weekly trash pickup and pay-as-you-throw mechanisms, weighing concerns about rodents, odors, and service cuts against municipal costs and the impact of curbside composting.
